memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Do not put the Lord your God to the test as you did at Massah. Be sure to keep the commands of the Lord your God and the stipulations and decrees he has given you. Do what is right and good in the Lord's sight, so that it may go well with you and you may go in and take over the good land the Lord promised on oath to your ancestors, thrusting out all your enemies before you, as the Lord said. - Deut 6:16-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses reminds Israel of Massah, where the thirsty people quarreled with God and demanded, "Is the Lord among us or not?" (Exod 17:7). To "test God" in this way is to demand that He prove Himself on our terms, to doubt His care and grumble against Him when circumstances turn hard. It springs from a heart that refuses to trust unless God performs on command. God calls His people instead to keep His commands and do what is right, trusting His goodness even when the way is difficult.

This is a real temptation for all of us. When life gets hard, we can slip into a bargaining, testing posture: "God, if You're really good, You'll do this for me." We put conditions on our trust and treat God as though He must answer to us. But faith does not demand that God prove Himself; faith rests in who He has already shown Himself to be.

Interestingly, Jesus quoted this very verse — "Do not put the Lord your God to the test" — when Satan tempted Him to force God's hand (Matt 4:7). Where Israel failed in the wilderness, Jesus perfectly trusted His Father. He is our example and our Savior. Because He trusted fully, we can lean on Him when our own trust falters. Instead of testing God, we can rest in His proven faithfulness and simply do what is right and good in His sight.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I ever put conditions on my trust, demanding God prove Himself?
- How can I respond with faith rather than grumbling when life is hard?
- What does Jesus' perfect trust in the Father teach me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, forgive me for the times I have tested You, demanding You prove Yourself instead of trusting Your goodness. Help me rest in Your proven faithfulness and simply do what is right and good in Your sight. Amen.
